# Library test review rules

Scope: library unit tests run by `cargo test` (`cargo test --lib`) and their helpers. Benchmarks and wider integration tests are out of scope.

**Primary focus: determinism.** Same controlled inputs must verify the same contract, independent of test order, parallel activity, host state, and incidental timing.

## Review sequence

1. Read changed tests, setup/cleanup, and the exercised production path. Identify the contract and uncontrolled dependencies.
2. Check input control, state isolation, synchronization, then assertions and supported feature/platform/release configurations.
3. Test the smallest unit that owns the contract; mock its collaborators. For concurrency, verify invariants across explored schedules, not one fixed schedule.
4. Report only evidenced defects: cite the source, name the wrong outcome or uncontrolled dependency, and recommend the smallest coverage-preserving fix. Use existing seams and repository policy; skip style nits and unrelated legacy cleanup.

Passing CI, snapshots, stress reruns, or a closed bug do not prove determinism or a root-cause fix. Distinguish harness defects from product races; preserve security checks and meaningful assertions.

Do not fix library tests by adding broader integration tests or jobs. Such coverage requires a separate design document defining purpose, boundaries, prerequisites, isolation, and runtime budget.

## Rules

Use the applicable recommendation, not a fixed number of solutions.
Markers are search hints, not proof of a defect; check usage and imported aliases.

| Avoid | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Substring assertions instead of checking the result. Markers: `assert!(x.contains(...))`, `.contains(`. | Prefer full `insta` snapshots or exact string/structured equality. Control inputs; normalize only incidental values. Use `starts_with` for prefix contracts, checking any meaningful remainder. Use `contains` only when containment itself is the contract. |
| Negative tests that accept any error or generic error text. Markers: `.is_err()`, `.unwrap_err().to_string()`. | Use `.unwrap_err()`/`.expect_err()` and assert typed causes and fields after setup reaches the intended branch. Test exact error wording separately with deterministic inputs. |
| Boolean checks that discard values/errors or verify only nonempty output. Markers: `.is_ok()`, `.is_some()`, `.is_none()`, `assert!(!x.is_empty())`, `.success()`, `.failure()`. | For expected `Ok`/`Some`, use `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` and compare the value. For expected `None`, use `assert_eq!(actual, None)` or `let None = actual else { panic!("expected None") };`. Assert relevant state changes and side effects too. |
| Branching on the actual result instead of asserting one expected variant. Markers: `match actual`, `if let`, wildcard arms. | Use `let Enum::A(x) = actual else { panic!("expected A") };`, then assert the payload. Split distinct expected outcomes into separate cases; fail unexpected variants instead of adapting assertions to them. |
| Tests embedded in standard library examples under `<crate>/src/examples`. Markers: `src/examples/`, `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `#[cfg(test)]`. | Keep examples focused on demonstration. Put regression tests in library test modules exercised by the existing CI `cargo test` gate; do not count example-embedded tests as CI coverage. |
| Requiring a full pipeline for a utility test, or mocking the behavior being asserted. | Call the utility directly with deterministic mocked collaborators. Reports, probes, and policies can be mocked when they are dependencies, not the subject of the assertion. |
| Network services, host configuration, tool installation, sign-in, browsers, or developer credentials. Markers: `reqwest::`, `TcpStream::connect`, `Command::new`. | Mock service and host dependencies; determine assertions from controlled inputs, not machine configuration. |
| Unspecified collaborators silently succeeding or reaching the host. | Reject unexpected calls; script only scenario-required interactions. |
| Writing input fixtures to disk during test setup. Markers: `fs::write`, `File::create`, `write_all`, `create_dir_all`. | Prefer in-memory values, byte buffers, or injected readers. If a file fixture is required, commit it as source and read it unchanged (`include_str!`, `include_bytes!`, or a checked-in path). Do not generate fixture files at test runtime. |
| Shared mutable fixtures, caches, or target directories. | Own mutable state per test; share only immutable inputs. Isolate filesystem outputs when writing them is the behavior under test, not fixture setup. |
| Global-state interference or first-use ordering hidden by atomics, save/restore, or partial locks. Markers: `static`, `AtomicUsize`, `set_hook`, `thread_local!`, `set_global_default`, `rebuild_interest_cache`. | Inject owned state. Initialize unavoidable shared infrastructure deterministically before concurrent tests; isolate observations per test. Thread-local state works only if all observed work stays on that thread. Unavoidable global mutation needs separate test design; resetting state afterward does not prevent concurrent interference. |
| Process environment/cwd mutation or host-dependent fixture paths. Markers: `set_var`, `remove_var`, `set_current_dir`, `current_dir`. | Pass explicit environment and working-directory inputs; use synthetic paths for mocked I/O or stable checked-in fixture paths. |
| Wall-clock/random assertions or sleeps for ordering. Markers: `SystemTime::now`, `Instant::now`, `Utc::now`, `thread_rng`, `rand::rng`, `sleep`, `sleep_until`. | Inject a [tick](https://docs.rs/tick/latest/tick/) clock: use `tick::Clock::new_frozen` with test-only `test-util`; use `ClockControl` to advance time explicitly in timer tests. Seed/script randomness; synchronize with channels, barriers, or notifications. |
| Permission changes, lock races, mandatory privileges, or host-dependent filesystem metadata. Markers: `set_permissions`, `chmod`, `symlink`. | Mock filesystem operations/metadata or inject specific errors. Preserve production security checks instead of relaxing them for fixtures. |
| Test helpers in default APIs or mismatched feature/backend gates. Markers: `#[cfg(`, `[features]`, `default =`. | Keep private tests in their crate; gate exported helpers behind a non-default test-support feature, not workspace defaults. Align cfg/imports; check production consumers without test features and supported partial-feature combinations. |
| Slow/unbounded test work or machine-speed assertions. Markers: `.elapsed()`, `Duration::from_`, `timeout`, large iteration counts, `loom::model`. | Target under one second per test in ordinary `cargo test`, excluding compilation. Reduce fixtures/work and mock expensive dependencies. Bound loops and explored schedules while preserving the invariant; state exploration limits. Assert work bounds, not wall-clock cutoffs; deadlines are safety limits. |
| Running external processes or generated fake executables for test setup/assertions. Markers: `Command::new`, `.spawn()`, `.output()`, `.status()`, `.wait()`, `.wait_with_output()`, `.sh`, `.bat`. | Mock the process runner with scripted status/stdout/stderr; test command construction, parsing, and policy in-process. Actual execution requires a justified integration design, not improved subprocess plumbing. |
| Blanket Miri exclusions for one unsupported dependency. Markers: `cfg(not(miri))`, `cfg_attr(miri, ignore`. | Ignore only affected tests with reasons; keep unaffected tests enabled. |
| Untuned stress workloads under Miri. Markers: `stress`, repeated loops, large iteration counts, `cfg(miri)`. | Exclude stress workloads with a reasoned `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "...")]`, or carefully reduce Miri-specific workload and measure its runtime. Preserve a small invariant-focused Miri case; native speed does not predict interpreter cost. |
| Assertions tied to compiler implementation details. Markers: allocation counts, `Backtrace`, `#[inline`, `black_box`. | Assert observable library behavior across supported build profiles, not assumed stack layout, allocation count, or source-loop callsites. Only require such properties when they are the explicit API contract; `black_box` does not guarantee them. |
| Retries, longer sleeps, weaker assertions, ignored tests, or nonrecurrence presented as fixes. Markers: `retry`, `sleep`, `#[ignore]`. | Remove the evidenced uncontrolled dependency while preserving coverage. Keep unresolved product races under investigation. Temporary quarantine must name lost coverage, owner, and restoration condition. |
